ClickUp's P is now free again (Telemetry's own eventual migration can reclaim it).
- The real DigiSmith repo (MEMORY.md, .digismith/docs/) is untouched by either reassignment - it still calls this content W and Y internally. ClickUp is the single source of truth for this lettering; the codebase's own lettering is a separate, independent scheme.

lists.name: A.4: Configuration
lists.content:
DigiSmith's configuration mechanism: the per-folder config file, its optional global layer, the shared reader that every skill and hook uses, and the migration from the older files.

- The mechanism lives here. The settings in the file stay with the lineages that own them: profile (O.0), role (O.3), preference keys such as finish_option and ssh_key (O.1), voices (T).
- Why in A: the A.3 SessionStart hook and the O.0 profile mechanism both read the config, so the config sits below both of them.
- 2026-10-02: Created (Jack). First build: the centralized config file (DGS-141).
- A.4: 2026-10-03: Renumbered from A.2 to A.4 (Jack), because A.0 is now the Pavilion.

lists.name: B.3: Token Economics
lists.content:
Token Economics: what a model token really costs on each channel, and what each task cost or would cost.

- The big comparison: for each model (Claude first, then Kimi and others), the official API price, a subscription plan's price and its API-equivalent value, and third-party gateway prices (TokenReply, Chutes, relays), with the date and source of every number.
- How each channel counts and bills tokens (cache read and write, batch, multipliers), and how far each one can be trusted.
- Per task: the real token counts of each task and model, and a what-if cost on every channel.
- Part of the K family (real DigiSmith letter K, B.0: Maestro). Related repo items: K.4 token counter (scripts/token-counter/), K.7 vendor benchmark, the usage monitoring client (C.3: Accounts, Capacity). Billing on C.3 may move here.
- 2026-10-10: Created (Jack).

lists.name: C.1: Workbox
lists.content:
Workbox: herdr on a VPS or any dedicated server, where DigiSmith's workers and reviewers run.

- Worker slots, the roster, the runbook (.digismith/sessions/workbox.md), and the dg workbox commands in packages/workbox.
- Which account a worker uses is decided in C.3: Accounts, and which model in B.2. This lineage runs the workers.
- 2026-10-03: Created (Jack). Candidates to move in: VPS hosting tickets from B.1, DGS-131, DGS-151.

lists.name: C.2: CLI
lists.content:
The dg command line: the command framework, its conventions and its tests.

- Each command group belongs to the lineage of the feature it operates (dg clickup in D.3, dg depot in D.2, dg workbox in C.1).
  This lineage owns the shell they plug into.
- 2026-10-03: Created (Jack). Candidate to move in: DGS-117.

lists.name: C.3: Accounts
lists.content:
Accounts: the logins DigiSmith's workers run on, and which one a new worker gets.

- The seats (jack, dev0), which seat each worker uses, usage against the 5h and weekly limits, limit stops, exhausted marks and token handling.
- Submodule: Capacity (seats, usage and limit stops). Billing (cost per ticket, plans, extra usage) may join later.
- The manual is in the Workbox runbook (.digismith/sessions/workbox.md), "Choose the account for a new worker". Starting a worker is C.1: Workbox.
- 2026-10-03: Created (Jack). Candidate to move in: DGS-144.

It previously would have hosted "Delivery" (DigiSmith's real map letter D - merge -> release -> verification -> announcement), but that clan was never migrated yet, so ClickUp's D is sunset from Delivery and reused here for Depot instead (DigiSmith's real internal letter V).

lists.name: D.1: Runtime Services
lists.content:
Shared machine-wide runtime services other DigiSmith builds depend on, each managed through the same ensure/stop lifecycle pattern (mirroring the packages/ clone's ensure/refresh shape):

- OpenCode server (2026-08-28) - a single shared server backing every digismith:offload-implementer dispatch (previously one server per plan), started/tracked/stopped via ensure-opencode-server/stop-opencode-server.
- Agentic Bridge proxy (2026-09-11, map item K.9) - a local HTTP proxy (scripts/agentic-bridge/server.ts) that repairs TokenReply's kimi-k3 XTML tool-call leak into a genuine Anthropic tool_use block before Claude Code's own agentic loop sees it, via ensure-agentic-bridge/stop-agentic-bridge.

lists.name: D.2: CLI & Packaging
lists.content:
Depot's CLI and publishing surface - the tooling that exposes its managed resources to the command line and to npm:

- VPS session CLI (2026-09-11) - status/connect commands reconnecting to an already-provisioned Hetzner VPS's persistent claude tmux session over SSH. Internally superseded 2026-09-24 by letter X's herdr-based rewrite, but this is where the CLI surface originated.
- @digismith/cli npm package (2026-09-12) - publishes Depot's CLI as the digismith/dg binaries (packages/cli). Ownership later moved to letter U (2026-09-19).
- dg depot command group (2026-09-13) - dg depot clone|opencode|bridge ensure|refresh|stop, wrapping V.0's and V.1's own resources into the CLI via a shared process-lifecycle helper.

lists.name: D.3: ClickUp Channel
lists.content:
DigiSmith's ClickUp integration surface, organized under two milestones plus this lineage's own backlog:

- ClickUp Connector (milestone) - @digismith/clickup-client package plus the dg clickup CLI: read commands (V.6, 2026-09-24) and write commands (V.7, 2026-09-25).
- Clan Backfill (milestone) - tracks migrating the other 24 DigiSmith map letters (A-Y, excluding V) into ClickUp using this same Clan/Lineage/ticket/doc-attachment pattern, one clan at a time, at Jack's own pace.
- Standalone backlog tickets - the connector's own deferred future work: CLI gaps (list/folder creation, delete-task, PDF export), tech debt from V.7's review, consumer integration wiring, the Soveron cutover, historical backfill, and the pending npm publish.

lists.name: O.4: Foundation
lists.content: A per-repo behavior profile (standards subset, ticket/ephemeral/reporting on-off) that existing stages consult independently at their own trigger point. Storage: .digismith/profile (one-line profile name) + profiles/<name>.yml (flat domain: choice pairs) - the same pattern every later profile-gated feature (G.2's toolchain, H's preferences) reuses.

lists.name: O.1: Preferences Store
lists.content:
Folded in from real DigiSmith letter H (Preferences store) 2026-09-26 - H and O are both per-repo configuration mechanisms (O = static behavior flags from profiles/*.yml, H = dynamic settings decided through live interaction, stored in .digismith/preferences.yml), close enough in theme that Jack chose to file H under this clan as its own lineage rather than giving it a separate ClickUp clan. Only H's current/final meaning is covered here (Preferences store) - H's earlier retired meaning (Subagent-driven always, 2026-08-12 - 2026-09-04, folded into W.6/P.2) is not migrated, same rule already applied to Q and U during the Clan Backfill milestone setup.

- 2026-10-02: Storage moves to the A.4: Configuration file (DGS-141). O.1 keeps the preference keys (finish_option, ssh_key) and digismith:preferences.

lists.name: O.2: Tailoring
lists.content:
Tailoring of each DigiSmith profile: the behavior a profile changes beyond the flags in profiles/<name>.yml, such as its own skills, templates, rules and tools.

- Profiles: DigiSmith, Emma, Jazurite, Personal.
- Each ticket sets the Profile custom field (O: Profiling folder) to exactly one profile.
- Profile empty: the ticket changes the tailoring mechanism itself, so it affects every profile.
- The profile mechanism and its flags (profiles/*.yml) stay in O.0. Per-repo settings (.digismith/preferences.yml) stay in O.1. Session roles (maestro / worker / solo) are in O.3.
- 2026-10-02: Created (Jack). Maestro was planned here as a fifth profile the same day, then moved to O.3: Roles, because it is a session role, not a profile.

lists.name: O.3: Roles
lists.content:
Session roles: what a session does, next to its profile (which org's behavior applies, O.0). Like Kubernetes: the maestro is the control plane (the "master"), the workers are the nodes.

- Roles: maestro (a Desktop session that supervises herdr workers), worker (a terminal session in a herdr pane, started by a maestro), solo (Jack's direct sessions, neither of the two).
- This lineage owns the role question at session start and the setup for each role: the maestro's home folder (~/.digismith-depot/maestro/) and its claims, and the worker's environment (DIGISMITH_MAESTRO, auto mode, folder trust).
- Workers never get the role question: the maestro sets their role when it starts them.
- The profile mechanism and its flags stay in O.0. Per-profile tailoring stays in O.2.
- 2026-10-02: Created (Jack). First build: the maestro role (DGS-139, backlog/manager-orchestrator-profile.md).

lists.name: Imperium
lists.content:
The roadmap: DigiSmith's initiatives, epics and milestones. Normal tickets do not live here; each one lives in its clan's lineage list.

- Initiative: a group of epics for one goal (custom task type Initiative). Its epics are its subtasks.
- Epic: a body of work with an end (custom task type Epic). Its tickets stay in their clan lists and link to the epic.
- Milestone: a dated checkpoint (ClickUp Milestone type). Its description says "done when"; the tickets that must finish first block it.
- Each clan folder has its own Pavilion list for items that affect more than one of that clan's lineages, or the clan as a whole.
- 2026-10-10: Renamed from Town Hall to Imperium (Jack), and made the home of initiatives, epics and milestones only.
- 2026-09-27: Renamed from Pavilion to Town Hall. The name Pavilion moved down one level, to the clan-level lists.
